input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: All calls to the wrapped function now share and clear a single statistics dict (the one on wrapped_f) instead of each call getting its own copy's dict. Concurrent or nested calls overwrite and clear each other's stats.
- rationale: Trigger: a retry-decorated function is called from multiple threads, or recursively, at once. Mechanism: stats.clear() wipes the dict that an in-flight call's copy is still updating, and both calls write to the same dict. Impact: statistics (attempt_number, delay_since_first_attempt) are corrupted. A thread-local mechanism was previously used to avoid this.
critique: The finding identifies the same mechanism as the label: one statistics dict on the wrapper is shared and cleared on every call instead of each call getting its own. As a result, concurrent or nested calls wipe and corrupt each other's start_time and attempt_number stats.
